title: Purification and Textual Variants of 2 Cor 7
english: Another kind of ease and prosperity, as if based on the truth of a word, appears and exalts itself. With this same way of thinking, you should apply each subsequent thing spoken with its own opposition.

Still pretending to be sorrowful and poor and having nothing, by which we make poverty a virtue, we rejoice, being rich in good works and in every word and in all knowledge, as also enriching others according to the wealth that looks sharp (2 Cor 6:10); for he who has this is master of all things, possessing them. And it is also good to say regarding each of the unpleasing ones, that this which is upon the good and saving things has been said to me.

He who has taken much boldness for the sake of speaking before the readiness of the listeners says: our mouth has been opened and our heart has been enlarged toward you, O Corinthians (2 Cor 6:11-13); therefore you are also being constricted by an annoying ignorance. This does not come from us; for we ask you as children to render a recompense to us by enlarging your understanding for the reception of that which we offer you as instruction. But it is necessary to take up bowels here not sensible; for the word is not about bodily things but spiritual ones.

Wives are called spouses to men, more by ecclesiastical custom than by scriptural union (2 Cor 6:14-16). For indeed, he forbids heterogamy through the things set forth, writing: you shall not be yoked with the unbelieving, saying this only: let a faithful man not take an unbelieving wife. For you are under the good Jesus' yoke, but she is under the yoke of some evil one. Likewise, a woman having faith should not be joined to an idolater. He persuades one to abstain from heterogamy, bringing forward what will necessarily follow: what participation is there in righteousness and lawlessness? And the following. Since for the faithful has righteousness, and becomes light of the world under Christ, but the unbeliever is full of lawlessness, so that because of this he is to be laid as darkness to Belial—and this one is evil—it is not necessary for a part to have the faithful with the unbeliever. For he himself has been built as a temple of God, but the unbeliever is a temple of idols, whence since righteousness is a non-participant of lawlessness, the light has no fellowship with the darkness. But neither is there harmony with Christ toward Belial, nor is there any agreement of the temple of God with a temple of idols; one should not approach by such a marriage; for he who does this fills...

A faithful person participating in lawlessness, and also sharing in darkness, and running away toward the Devil, and greeting the unbelieving party. Therefore, let us flee all these things previously mentioned, being temples of the spoken God; I will dwell in them and walk about in them. For if you become sons and daughters of God, set apart from the unclean unbelievers, do not lay yourselves under the same yoke so that you might happen to obtain these holy rewards, having cleansed yourselves from all defilements of the flesh arising from heterogamy; for then you will practically and in thinking accomplish holiness of the Spirit. 2 Cor 7:1

The preceding word stands differently. For some read: 'Therefore, having these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, so that we may not have a defilement of sin from neither flesh nor spirit, that is, of the soul or of the mind; for then it will necessarily follow to accomplish in the fear of the Lord holiness, so as to be holy in spirit and body.' Others, reading 'let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit,' separate 'and spirit' [as] 'accomplishing holiness.' They maintain this distinction, those who wish, the 'holy Spirit' which is brought forth in the Scriptures without an addition; for they say the Scripture intends to show this, wherever it is 'holy Spirit of God' or something else so called. But also without an addition, as in the case where the Spirit itself bears witness to our spirit, whereas the opposite, with an addition, is always called thus: an unclean spirit, an evil spirit, a spirit of a demon, or perhaps something else with an addition. 2 Cor 7:2-5

He who is about to speak with boldness along with those sending the letter, says to the Corinthians: 'Make room, that is, make space for us to be defending ourselves. We have become guilty of no injustice, nor corruption, nor greed toward any of you. And these things I speak with boldness, not desiring to condemn you; for I had testified that you are so ready as to die for us. And so are we for you; for such a readiness of purpose was prepared in our hearts and in yours. Therefore, having much boasting over you, I am full of consolation, the joy of your salvation and gladness overflowing in us...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Joy of Obedience and the Equality of Giving
english: Everyone for whom we suffer on behalf of the truth will harm us. For even when they had come to Macedonia, our flesh had no respite from the constantly attacking trials. However, even if the flesh has no respite, we are being born by the Spirit, since we are not distressed even if we are being squeezed in every way.

Interpreting what those distressing [things] were, he brought forward that there were battles indeed from without, but fears from within. And this is understood in two ways: first, it must be said that there exist battles from without for the apostles from those wishing to persecute and influence, but fears from within for those within the church who seem to be steadfast and unshakeable; for they feared the instability of the Corinthians, being quickly carried away from the doctrines of the truth, whence he says to them: 'I fear lest, as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness, your minds be corrupted' (2 Cor 11:3). Alternatively, the external battle might be understood as this: that the uprisings against us are occurring; those from without press us without leaving space until they disturb the heart. However, even if the soul is undisturbed, there are fears within concerning falling away; for we are liable to be turned.

The God who gives grace to the lowly consoles them, offering encouragement, so that they may bear the heavy things with endurance (2 Cor 7:6); he also comforted us in the arrival of Titus from you to us (2 Cor 7:7). And it was not only his presence that comforted, but also the promise concerning you; for he spoke of the zeal which you showed toward him according to God. He also extended to us the news of those who know joy, how much great disposition and compassion he is exceeding to save toward you. Along with these, he promised that you have zeal and lamentation and longing on my behalf, so as to no longer hesitate concerning the fact that you had been left from the reproofs of the former letter; for I learned from his words that the sorrow, having existed for a little while from what was written, has become a seed and the greatest occasion for joy (2 Cor 7:10).

Regarding having wronged, he says the father's wife has [wronged], or having been wronged, either the father whom he had as a wife even if he has died, or the law which forbids such a marriage (2 Cor 7:12); for it was, even if previously their consent had occurred, not a common [matter] but looking toward those to write a letter.

It must be sought, not for their sake, but so that your zeal may be known through the spoken word having been inscribed for the purpose of obeying; for concerning this I always boast, exhorting the Macedonians to the same zeal. Indeed, it was necessary, so that I might not be ashamed of you having received sorrow not properly. Since therefore it did not happen so, but according to God you having grieved, as much as much, followed by repentance, I rejoice and am confident in all such things in you.

Through this joy, our encouragement and consolation were increased, with Titus testifying concerning your zeal with holiness (2 Cor 7:13-15), for he says the spirit rests from your obedience, especially since he found it so, just as I always announced to him concerning your obedience. The spirit rests somewhat when, from those who are the causes of rest, one receives according to piety and virtue and a faithful mindset according to the truth, those who receive the pleasant things of life from those who gladden, resting according to the flesh and not according to the spirit.

For Titus constantly restores us by announcing your beautiful obedience; and this itself becomes a cause of delight, because just as we were seen always speaking with the truth. The word of piety does not compel one to give what one does not have, but what one has should be provided willingly (2 Cor 8:10-15). And this will be easily accomplished when they see who are the partakers; for these are holy and God's healers. Therefore we also hope that an exchange will be; for they are sufficient to provide spiritual things instead of the sensible things they receive. For thus equality will be even in the present time, as it happened during the giving of the manna, neither the one having little being diminished nor the one having much exceeding; for inequality remains when, those having heavenly things of the saints, and you having earthly things, no exchange takes place. Therefore, sow carnal things, participating in the needs of the saints, so that you may reap from them the spiritual; for thus there will be equality in your receiving from the great and from those who are small; for you shall have the great things with the small, and they the small things with the great. And this equality will exist according to restorative justice.
I write these things, not defending myself to you—for I know how you contend concerning us—but so that we might not only (2 Cor 8:24)...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Spiritual Warfare against Sophistic Falsehood
english: We intend to have good works before the Lord and also before men. For it is certain what intention we serve God with, this is not doubted; but it is also proper to care for men, so that one must strive not to be deceived by impostors and sophists. It must be understood that the one placing before himself to please God first and then men is not a man-pleaser, but having pre-determined only this: to live acceptably toward mortals, even if God does not accept him. And having praised him from his own correct actions, and having lifted him up because of the love toward those, he is pre-setting seeds for them of the love toward the Corinthians, so that by this also the contribution might become greater. And since he has moreover demonstrated to them his virtue, he exhorts also those under them.

I, even I, the teacher of you and writing the things set forth, exhort according to the virtue which Christ has given me—and it is gentleness and forbearance (2 Kor 10:1)—to be more courageous, though finding it long to be in your subjection, as if I had appeared lowly when present; for when, having arrived, I find the things of the exhortation turned into works, I will moderate my mind with much gentleness among you (2 Kor 10:2). Therefore I beg that, being present, you do not be so courageous as to bear the face of a teacher rebuking and striking, so that I may not be compelled by the confidence in a teacher to dare, according to some thinking, to walk according to the flesh. Or should someone think that we live according to the flesh, when it is perceived that these things we have written not for the sake of the matter, but so that we might be thought to be some great ones, being obedient to you and becoming ones contributing more? For God testifies, and more men, that the counsel has happened for the sake of the ministry becoming abundant, and not for the sake of any other human (2 Kor 10:3).

The thing set forth has the sense of what is written in another epistle, having thus: we have our citizenship in heaven, though we walk on earth (Phil 3:20); for it would be the same to walk according to the flesh and on earth, and not to fight according to the flesh, to have the citizenship in heaven (2 Kor 10:4-7). But when he says to fight according to the flesh, he does not mean all those prepared for war, but rather even the fleshly ones and therefore having been acted upon by sin, such as were those about whom it has been said: it shall not remain the...

My spirit is among these men because they are flesh. Having risen above these, they fight again according to the flesh against Christ, the King of all. Therefore, in order to please the one who fights, they do not involve themselves in the affairs of life, that is, the material things.

For certainly, the weapons they carry are not perceptible and bodily—for these are weak—but they are powerful to God. For those using these things cast down the strongholds of the deceitful words most sophistically constructed by the heterodox, and also the things exalted in these words against the knowledge of God. For those opposing the knowledge of truth, introducing impious and atheistic doctrines, building strong fortresses with the intensity of words, and finding space within them, think they are invincible. Toward these things, which they present as if through teaching with apparent proof, they bring a vain loftiness, exalting false thought as if it contains more than the ecclesiastical opinion called 'knowledge of God'. For He Himself provides to those worthy.

Therefore, in order to cast down the aforementioned exaltations and strongholds, having put on the armor of God according to the spirit, we fight in the said manner. For we dissolve their sophistic words and refute their doctrines. Certainly, every thought of the deceived held by the deceivers, but also having it overturned in their own land, we bring it toward obeying Christ.

It is possible to take it also in this way: every thought brought in any teaching, we bring by necessity and force, relocating it toward persuading them to obey Christ. For just as the inscription lying on the altar in Athens shows the thought of many gods, he who writes these things has drawn it toward the only true God, saying: 'Whom not knowing, you worship; this I proclaim to you.' But the inscription showed a multitude of gods. Therefore, when every thought is captured into obedience to Christ, we will be ready to bring such a thing as a vengeance against all disobedience, just as captives, having taken a certain nation in victory, become bold to undermine the land of those people.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
